title: Beyond the Bean: A Nordic Perspective on Circular Food Systems

findings.claim: The Nordic region's economy is only 6% circular
findings.locator: seksjon 'Nordics Need to Tackle Food Waste on the Production Side'

findings.claim: Nordic countries make up only 0.33% of the total global population (2024)
The Nordic region makes up the 12th-largest economy in the world
Finland was the first country in the world to adopt a national circular economy roadmap

notMeasured: Ingen egne primærdata; syntese/omtale med kilder til NNR2023 og Circularity Gap Report 2024
limitations: Omtaleartikkel skrevet med PACE; tall fra tredjepartsrapporter.

title: New report: Nordic public companies compete for circularity (Circular Economy Outlook for the Nordics 2024)

findings.claim: 79% of companies believe competitors will develop significant circular capabilities within coming years
42% have defined a target for at least one circular strategy; less than a third measure progress
The Circular Business Index for Nordic public companies is 21% (max 100%)
findings.systemBoundary: beregnet indeks over alle deltakende børsnoterte selskaper

findings.claim: One-fifth of companies set circular purchase requirements only when customers/authorities demand it

notMeasured: Landing er pressemelding; rapport-PDF ikke hentet (bak nedlastingsskjema)
limitations: Pressemelding/omtale; %-tall er survey-svar, indeksen er en beregning.

title: NORSØK joins major European initiative for circular food systems: CIRCULANDIA

findings.claim: CIRCULANDIA links value chains for local food production, organic waste and packaging; NORSØK adapts methods to Møre og Romsdal (demonstrator/replicator learning-system)
findings.systemBoundary: regional (Møre og Romsdal) lokal matproduksjon + organisk avfall + emballasje

notMeasured: Ingen kvantitative resultat-/volumtall; prosjektbeskrivelse ved oppstart

title: A Perspective of Upcycled Food by Norwegian Consumers: The Meaning Without the Word

findings.claim: Focus-group study identified 76 words/concepts Norwegian consumers associate with upcycled food; 'sustainability' predominant
findings.locator: abstract (J. Int. Food & Agribusiness Marketing, s.1-25)

findings.claim: Four themes (Culture, Resource Utilization, Innovation, Ultra-processed) via five codes incl. 'Food waste','Lack of knowledge'

notMeasured: Ingen kvantitativ forbruker-survey; rent kvalitativ studie
limitations: Fagfellevurdert; curl 403, metadata/abstrakt via WebFetch; full tekst bak forlag.

title: FeedLoop — redesign of local food systems in Tolga and Steinkjer

findings.claim: FeedLoop (2025-2027, Research Council of Norway) redesigns local food systems around Tolga/Steinkjer to reduce feed-food competition using livestock on non-food biomass/by-products
findings.systemBoundary: lokale matsystemer rundt Tolga og Steinkjer

title: Circular Food Pilot — household food waste reduction (NO/SE/FI/DE/EE)

findings.claim: Every year 59 million tons of food are wasted in Europe (cited: European Commission)
Globally food waste accounts for 8-10% of GHG emissions (cited: UNEP Food Waste Index 2021)
Pilot runs in five CCRI regions: Finland, Sweden, Norway, Germany, Estonia
Pilot target: reduce food waste by 50% among participating households

notMeasured: 50% er pilotmål, ikke resultat; 59Mt og 8-10% er siterte tredjepartstall

title: Nutricycle/Columbi Farms — truly circular decoupled aquaponics (manifest-URL nutricycle.no DØD)

findings.claim: Columbi Farms claims up to 9 kg edible greens per 1 kg salmon by reusing nutrients from fish farms
findings.systemBoundary: decoupled akvaponi (RAS smolt + hydroponisk vertikalfarm), projisert/selskapsanslag

findings.claim: Nutricycle (Columbi Farms, SINTEF Nord, NIBIO, Salmar; Forskningsrådet) gjenvinner nitrat/fosfor/kalium fra akvakultur-avløpsvann; pilot ved NIBIO Landvik

notMeasured: Manifest-URL nutricycle.no død (Wix, 404). 9 kg/kg kun fra søkesnutt, ikke sideverifisert; columbifarms.no ECONNREFUSED
limitations: Primærlanding død; funn fra substituttkilder. Yield-tall er projeksjon, må verifiseres.

source: Renewable Matter (Emanuele Bompan) — ref. Circularity Gap Report Norway (Circle Economy & Circular Norway)
title: Norway has a long way to become circular. Here is why

findings.claim: The Norwegian economy is only 2.4% circular
Global average circularity 8.6%; Austria 9.7%; Netherlands 24.5%
97.6% of materials consumed each year never make it back into the Norwegian economy
Norway per-capita material consumption 44.3 tonnes/person
With the right interventions Norway could see a 20-fold increase in circularity

limitations: Artikkel datert 2020-08-28 (manifest oppga 2024 — avvik); tall fra Circularity Gap Report Norway 2020.

title: Circular food in practice: Collaboration for sustainable public meals

findings.claim: The Swedish public meal system serves ~3 million meals a day to pupils, hospital patients and elderly

limitations: RISE-siden blokkerte curl og WebFetch (CAPTCHA). Metadata fra WebSearch-sammendrag.

title: Carlsberg Sverige leads circular economy push by turning beer dredge into food (Brewed & Renewed)

findings.claim: Sweden generates ~80,000 tonnes of brewers' spent grain ('dredge') per year, most used for animal feed, biogas or composting
Brewed & Renewed (RISE-led; Carlsberg Sverige, Axfood, Axfoundation, Bagerigruppen, Elajo, Fazer) upcycles spent grain into bread/cereals

notMeasured: Ingen andel av dredge faktisk oppgradert til mat; kun total biproduktmengde
limitations: Bransjeartikkel datert 2025-03-25 (manifest oppga 2024). 80 000 tonn aktøropplysning uten metode.

title: Circular food system in Gottsunda Center — From food waste to sustainable profitability

findings.claim: Today, up to 30% of all produced food is wasted
Project target: reduce food waste in Gottsunda Centre by up to 50% by 2026
Expected up to 15% better margins for restaurants and at least 3% for retailers

notMeasured: Alle tall er mål/projeksjoner, ikke måleresultater
limitations: Prosjektside; 30% generell påstand, 50/15/3% er mål mot 2026.

title: Rethinking Food: From byproducts to breakthroughs (Dr Aratrika Ray)

findings.claim: Researcher profile: Dr Aratrika Ray (KTH) transforms food waste into resources via biopolymers/carbohydrate chemistry within PLENTY circular-food programme

title: Designing a More Sustainable Future: Annelise de Jong research journey

findings.claim: Researcher profile: Dr Annelise de Jong (KTH/IVL) combines design, behaviour and systems thinking on sustainable consumption incl. food, within PLENTY
